title: Ivo and the Protocol
premise: Paloma Voss smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers along the silent corridor between Earth and the colony world Meridian, keeping his head down and his past locked away. When Meridian's children begin dreaming a shared dream — a message from the long-lost third colony, Ashfall, presumed dead — Paloma realizes the contraband he's been carrying for years is fragments of that message, scattered deliberately by someone who trusted no one else to deliver it whole. Hunted by Earth's enforcers and Meridian's desperate council alike, Paloma assembles an unlikely crew of smugglers, defectors, and one of the dreaming children to carry the message home. In the end, delivering it means surrendering his own sealed memories to prove the truth: the war was engineered by those who profited from silence. The colonies reunite, and Paloma — who never belonged anywhere — finally comes home.
about_author: Jude Sterling is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing voices of people the world forgot. They write science fiction about memory, exile, and the families we build when the official ones fail us.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Paloma runs contraband memories through orbital customs at Meridian, narrating his careful rituals of invisibility. He delivers a wafer to a nervous client and pockets his fee, telling himself he carries nothing that matters. The beat is weary competence masking loneliness; we learn he hasn't spoken to Earth in nine years.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Sleep
chapters.summary: Meridian POV shifts to Sefi, age eleven, who wakes screaming from a dream of burning orange fields — and finds forty other children dreamed it too. Her teacher reports it; the council seals the school. Emotional beat: uncanny dread, and Sefi's stubborn insistence that the dream was a message, not a symptom.

chapters.title: Contraband That Whispers
chapters.summary: Paloma discovers one of his old wafers has degraded into something alive with signal — fragments matching the children's dream. His supplier, the dying smuggler Anselm, confesses he's been seeding the route for years. Beat: betrayal curdling into awe; Paloma realizes he's been a courier all along without knowing it.

chapters.title: Anselm's Last Run
chapters.summary: Anselm dies before explaining everything, leaving Paloma a ledger of wafer drop-points across three systems and a warning: Earth's enforcers already know. Paloma must choose between burning the ledger and following it. Beat: grief and the first pull toward purpose; he keeps the ledger.

chapters.title: Customs House Blues
chapters.summary: Enforcer Captain Ilsa Reyne interrogates Paloma at customs, courteous and lethal, showing him footage of Anselm's death labeled 'accident.' Paloma lies well but leaves shaken, knowing she let him go on purpose — a hook, not mercy. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wouldn't Forget
chapters.summary: Sefi escapes the sealed school and stows away on Paloma's ship, the Kestrel, carrying a drawing of the dream: a tower under orange skies. Paloma tries to turn her in and can't. Beat: reluctant connection; two people who don't belong anywhere recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Wafers Remember
chapters.summary: Paloma plays the recovered fragments: voices speaking a dialect from Ashfall, the colony declared lost forty years ago. The message is incomplete — seven wafers remain scattered. Beat: wonder and dread braided together; the war's founding lie begins to crack open.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Paloma recruits disgraced xenolinguist Dr. Amara Okafor and washed-up pilot Dev Chandra, assembling a crew of exiles. Each joins for a different wound. Beat: found family taking shape around a shared secret; warmth threaded with distrust.

chapters.title: The Drop at Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: First retrieval: a wafer hidden inside a decommissioned station shrine. Ilsa Reyne ambushes them; they escape by venting cargo and nearly lose Sefi. Beat: action and cost — Paloma learns this mission will demand more than cleverness.

chapters.title: Sefi's Dream, Deeper
chapters.summary: Under Amara's guidance, Sefi re-enters the shared dream consciously and returns with coordinates and a name: Warden Essu, last voice of Ashfall. Beat: intimacy and fear; the child becomes the mission's heart, and Paloma becomes her protector in fact.

chapters.title: Earth Sends Its Regards
chapters.summary: Ilsa corners the Kestrel and offers Paloma amnesty to hand over the wafers — revealing Earth knew Ashfall survived and chose silence to keep the colonies dependent. He refuses. Beat: love against duty inverted; Ilsa, herself dutiful, lets him go and questions her own side.

chapters.title: The Orange Fields
chapters.summary: A retrieved fragment shows Ashfall alive but failing — terraforming collapse, a population rationing its own memories to survive. The message is a plea and an offer of reconciliation. Beat: heartbreak; the stakes become human, not political.

chapters.title: Dev's Debt
chapters.summary: Dev's old smuggling partners sell the Kestrel's route to Earth for leniency. Ambushed at a fuel depot, the crew barely escapes; the ship is crippled. Beat: betrayal within the found family, and forgiveness — Dev confesses, and Paloma chooses trust over rage.

chapters.title: Amara's Translation
chapters.summary: Amara cracks the message's final layer: it isn't just a plea — it contains proof of who engineered the war, encoded in Ashfall's memory-rationing records. Delivering it will topple governments. Beat: dread of consequence; the crew votes to continue anyway.

chapters.title: Ilsa Reyne Defects
chapters.summary: Isla arrives not with guns but with evidence Earth plans to sterilize Ashfall rather than admit the truth. She begs to join. Paloma must decide whether duty can ever be trusted again. Beat: uneasy alliance; enemies becoming something like kin.

chapters.title: The Silence Between Worlds
chapters.summary: The final wafer lies in Earth-space itself, in the archive where Paloma's own sealed memories are stored. To retrieve it, he must unseal himself — exposing why he fled Earth nine years ago. Beat: confrontation with the self; he agrees.

chapters.title: Paloma Unsealed
chapters.summary: Paloma's memories return: he was Ashfall-born, evacuated as a child, his testimony about the war's engineering buried and erased. He has been carrying the message in his own head all along. Beat: devastating revelation; the smuggler was always the cargo.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: The Kestrel makes a desperate run through Earth's blockade toward Ashfall, Sefi broadcasting the dream to every colony child as a living beacon. Casualties mount; the ship breaks. Beat: climax rising — sacrifice, velocity, hope against impossible odds.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: They land among the orange fields. Warden Essu receives the complete message — Paloma's testimony plus the archive proof — and broadcasts it to both worlds simultaneously. Beat: catharsis; the truth lands like sunrise after a forty-year night.

chapters.title: The War That Ends
chapters.summary: Earth's command fractures as the proof spreads; enforcers stand down colony by colony. Ilsa testifies. The councils of three worlds convene for the first time in a generation. Beat: aftermath and reckoning; justice arriving imperfectly but truly.

chapters.title: Home Is a Crew
chapters.summary: Repairs, funerals, and a festival in the orange fields. Sefi asks Paloma if he'll stay; he realizes the Kestrel's crew is the first family he never had to smuggle. Beat: belonging earned, not granted; quiet joy.

chapters.title: The Next Message
chapters.summary: Months later, a new signal arrives from deeper space — another lost colony, another dream beginning. Paloma, Sefi, and the crew of the rebuilt Kestrel set out together, couriers now by choice. Beat: hopeful forward motion; the story ends where it began, but no longer alone.
